tasks.short: Confer with staff to plan and schedule curriculum-aligned lessons

steps.what: Confer with staff to agree lesson aims, sequence and curriculum alignment
Arrange agreed lessons against staff, room and timetable availability
Check the final lesson schedule and confirm arrangements with staff

tasks.design: Retain staff agreement on curriculum and lesson sequence. Configure shared availability and reusable schedule entries in {CALENDAR}, linked to the agreed lesson plan in {LMS}; the teacher resolves exceptions and confirms the exact schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated availability messages can slow scheduling after the educational plan is agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calendars can consolidate availability without choosing educational priorities.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling learning sequence with staffing and room constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a convenient slot would undermine the agreed lesson plan.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated scheduling; curriculum and timetable authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate a curriculum sequence across classes

evidence.claim: Native shared calendars can reduce repeated availability collation while leaving curriculum agreement and exception resolution human.

assumptions: Boundary covers this teacher's lesson-planning discussion and scheduling, not colleagues' participation or central timetable construction. Overlap with programme collaboration is allocated once.

In s1 the teacher captures agreed topic, aim, duration, sequence dependency, staff and resource needs. Timetable and room owners supply existing availability and fixed constraints outside this boundary, unchanged; retained s2 time includes field entry, checking availability and contacting staff with incomplete calendars.
Missing constraints or conflicts return to manual coordination; a free slot never overrides curriculum sequence or delegated timetable limits.
Test native calendar and schedule views before custom automation. No model chooses pupil level, staff allocation or educational content.
The time split is an E1 scenario to validate.
unknowns: Calendar coverage, schedule authority and actual coordination burden
research_questions: Does shared availability reduce messaging after counting requirement capture and conflicts?

already_counted.description: Educational agreement and final schedule confirmation remain.
Schedule entry, conflict checks and manual contacts remain.

incremental.description: Teacher checks recurring availability and schedule-rule problems.

approvals.approved_version: Exact lessons, staff, rooms, dates, times and sequence checked against the agreed requirements; changes require renewed confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less two focal upkeep hours gives net=8. High assumes scheduling halves; low assumes missing calendars and conflicts leave only upkeep-equivalent gains. Curriculum discussion and final confirmation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend professional meetings, conferences and teacher training

steps.what: Attend professional meetings, educational conferences and teacher training workshops and participate actively

tasks.design: Retain active participation in professional learning. Existing {LMS} material may support the session, but a generated summary does not replace attendance, discussion or practice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Professional learning requires attention, reflection and interaction.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital material can support access without proving equivalent learning from skipped participation.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what transfers to this classroom and practising a new skill.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a relevant question and challenge an idea against real teaching experience.
tasks.altitude: No change to learning responsibility or attendance time.

reach.task: Discuss a training idea's relevance to the curriculum

evidence.claim: Active attendance and professional learning are not removed by generating notes or summaries.

assumptions: Boundary is session participation, not booking, travel or a separate training report. Provider preparation and facilitation are outside and unchanged.

The provider supplies the existing programme and materials; the teacher produces questions and learning through participation in s1. No structured competence gain is assumed or inferred from attendance.
Missing understanding requires questions or practice within retained learning time. Native learning-resource access is considered first; no new tool is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because participation and tools are unchanged.
unknowns: Training mix and which activities require practical participation
research_questions: Which professional learning activities change classroom practice after participation?

already_counted.description: All attendance, discussion and learning remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Conferences and practical workshops retain active participation time; no summary-based attendance saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Organise and supervise games and recreational development activities

steps.what: Organise games and recreational activities, participants, space and equipment for developmental goals
Supervise games and recreation and adapt participation to support students' development

tasks.design: Retain practical organisation and supervision with the teacher. Existing activity guidance in {DOCS} can support selection, but a generated game plan does not set up equipment, include a hesitant student or maintain safety.
tasks.previous_blocker: The activity must fit the real space, group and changing participation.
tasks.enabler_now: Resource access does not remove practical organisation or supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing challenge, inclusion and safety in the moment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice exclusion or conflict and adapt the activity constructively.
tasks.altitude: No change in supervision responsibility or activity time.

reach.task: Seek an inclusive modification to a recreational activity
reach.learn: Accessible participation and limits of general classroom adaptations

evidence.claim: Practical activity setup and responsive supervision remain physical and relational work.

assumptions: Boundary covers practical organisation and live supervision, not a distinct written lesson-plan task.

The teacher assesses the space, equipment, group needs and activity rules in s1, including all preparation time. No structured safe-activity flag or complete participation profile is assumed; uncertainty requires direct checking and adaptation.
Native activity resources are reviewed before future custom tools; none is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new software or capture is proposed. Supervision overlapping other school duties is allocated once.
unknowns: Activity setting, equipment and available specialist support
research_questions: Which recurring participation barriers need a specialist activity modification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Familiar games and activities needing adaptation retain setup and supervision; no physical work is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist in the library and supervise halls, cafeteria or bus transitions

steps.what: Perform assigned library assistance, hall or cafeteria monitoring, or bus loading and unloading supervision

tasks.design: Retain the assigned duty with a present adult who assists students and responds to events. Existing duty information in {CALENDAR} supports assignment, but this task's hall, cafeteria, library and bus work is direct service and supervision.
tasks.previous_blocker: The duty requires physical presence and a response to unpredictable events.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital rosters can show assignments without carrying them out.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing a developing problem and assisting safely during busy transitions.
tasks.human_edge: Respond to a student's need and intervene with proportionate judgement.
tasks.altitude: No change in assigned supervision or assistance time.

reach.task: Support safe and orderly student use of the library
reach.learn: Local library procedures and when to refer a request

evidence.claim: Present-adult school supervision and practical assistance cannot be counted as removed by a digital duty roster.

assumptions: This single step represents one assigned duty period; the listed duties are alternatives, not a sequence. Boundary excludes producing the duty roster or a separate incident report.

School duty owners produce location, time and responsibility through existing assignment work outside this boundary, unchanged. The teacher checks conditions and carries out the duty in s1; no structured safety feed or free incident classification is assumed.
Unclear instructions are clarified through the existing school route. Native roster access is considered first; no tool change is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the task remains unchanged. The word administrative does not make these physical duties removable clerical time.
unknowns: Actual duty allocation and division of library assistance
research_questions: Does the measured duty period contain a distinct clerical action beyond direct assistance and supervision?

already_counted.description: All assigned direct supervision and assistance remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Quiet duty periods and incidents both retain adult presence and assistance; existing roster runtime yields no labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native shared scheduling may reduce a limited part of coordination. Professional learning, recreation supervision and school duties retain their human time.
reach: Coordinate curriculum sequences with instructional coordinators
Seek inclusive activity advice from adapted physical education specialists
Support library technicians within local procedures
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with clearer shared lesson arrangements who remains present for learning, development and safe school transitions.
